title: FY 2025 Survey
fullTitle: Higher Education Research and Development (HERD) Survey, Short Form
changesNote: There were no changes to this questionnaire from the FY 2024 version.

content.html: This survey collects data on research and development (R&D) activities at higher education institutions. Please report R&D activities and expenditures for your institution's 2025 fiscal year.

content.text: Fiscal year (FY)
Please report data for your institution's 2025 fiscal year.
Research and Development (R&D)

R&D activity is creative and systematic work undertaken in order to increase the stock of knowledge — including knowledge of humankind, culture, and society — and to devise new applications of available knowledge. R&D covers three activities defined below — basic research, applied research, and experimental development.

items.text: is experimental or theoretical work undertaken primarily to acquire new knowledge of the underlying foundations of phenomena and observable facts, without any particular application or use in view.
is original investigation undertaken in order to acquire new knowledge. It is directed primarily towards a specific, practical aim or objective.

is systematic work, drawing on knowledge gained from research and practical experience and producing additional knowledge, which is directed to producing new products or processes or to improving existing products or processes.

content.text: R&D Expenditures

Include all expenditures for R&D activities from your institution’s current operating funds that are separately accounted for. For purposes of this survey, R&D includes expenditures for organized research as defined by 2 CFR Part 200 Appendix III and expenditures from funds designated for research.

rows:
• Sponsored research (federal and nonfederal)
  • University research (institutional funds that are separately budgeted for individual R&D projects)
  • Startup, bridge, or seed funding provided to researchers within your institution
  • Other departmental funds designated for research
  • Recovered and unrecovered indirect costs (see definitions in Question 1)
  • Equipment purchased from R&D project accounts
  • R&D funds passed through to a subrecipient organization, educational or other
  • Clinical trials, Phases I, II, or III (see definition in Question 5)
  • Research training grants funding work on organized research projects
  • Tuition remission provided to students working on research

• Public service grants or outreach programs
  • Curriculum development (unless included as part of an overall research project)
  • R&D conducted by university faculty or staff at outside institutions that is not accounted for in your financial records
  • Estimates of the proportion of time budgeted for instruction that is spent on research
  • Capital projects (i.e., construction or renovation of research facilities)
  • Non-research training grants
  • Unrecovered indirect costs that exceed your institution’s federally negotiated Facilities and Administrative (F&A) rate

content.text: Reporting Units

columns: Please include these components of your institution:
rows:
• All units of your institution included in or with your financial statements, such as:
    • Agricultural experiment stations
    • Branch campuses
    • Medical schools
    • Hospitals or clinics
    • Research centers and facilities
    • A university 501(c)3 foundation

• Federally Funded R&D Centers (FFRDCs). This information is collected separately. See the list of FFRDCs: http://www.nsf.gov/statistics/ffrdc/.
  • Other organizations or institutions, such as teaching hospitals or research institutes, with which your institution has an affiliation or relationship, but which are not components of your institution.
  • Other campuses headed by their own president, chancellor, or equivalent within your university system. Each campus is asked to respond separately.

content.text: Primary Contact Information
Please complete the contact information for the person responsible for the survey
Mailing Address

At the end of each survey cycle, we send a thank-you letter to the president/chancellor of each institution that completes the survey. In that letter, we acknowledge the person listed as the primary contact. If there are other individuals who should also be thanked in the letter, please let us know in the box below. Please limit to 2 individuals, and provide first and last names and job titles.
Other Contact Information
List individuals who should be copied on all e-mails about the survey or can create a login account.

items: Check All Email box, if this person should be copied on all e-mails.
Check Can Log In box, if this person can create a login account. After you save the information on this page, this person will receive an e-mail allowing them to create their own password.
Job Title should include information about office/department as appropriate (e.g., VP of Sponsored Programs, Department of Finance Manager, Analyst II in Grants Management).

content.html:
• In rows a, b, c, d, and f: Include both direct and recovered indirect costs (reimbursement of F&A costs from external sponsors).
  • Report the original source of funds, when possible.
  • Funds coming through your institution's 501(c)3 should be reported based on the original funding source (e.g., restricted gifts in row f; unrestricted gifts in row e).
  • Include all fields of R&D (e.g., sciences, engineering, humanities, education, law, arts).

content.label: U.S. federal government
description: Any agency of the United States government.
Include federal funds passed through from another institution. Funds from FFRDCs should be treated as direct federal funding.

content.label: State and local government
description: Any state, county, municipality, or other local government entity in the United States, including state health agencies.
Include state funds that support R&D at agricultural and other experiment stations.
Public institutions should report state appropriations restricted for R&D activities here rather than in row e, Institutional funds.

content.label: Business
description: Domestic or foreign for-profit organizations. Report funds from a company's nonprofit foundation in row d.

content.label: Nonprofit organizations
description: Domestic or foreign nonprofit foundations and organizations, except universities and colleges. Funds from other universities and colleges should be reported in row f.

children.label: Institutionally financed research
description: Separately accounted for R&D funded by your institution. Do not include estimated research time. Exclude institution research administration and support (e.g., office of sponsored programs) or other indirect costs.

children.text: Did you include the following types of funding in your responses to Question 1, row e1?

items.label: Competitively awarded internal grants for research
items.description: Expenditures for organized research projects, involving a proposal or statement of work with expected research outcomes.

items.label: Startup packages/bridge funding/seed funding
items.description: Expenditures from funds provided to faculty members to begin or continue their research while seeking external sponsors.

items.label: Other departmental funds designated for research
items.description: Expenditures for research from other departmental or central accounts which do not match the descriptions provided in rows a or b.

items.label: Tuition assistance for student research personnel
items.description: University tuition assistance, waivers, or remission provided to students working on organized research. Please check "Included" even if these funds are reported as part of the expenditures included under rows a, b, or c.

children.label: Cost sharing
description: Include committed cost sharing other than unrecovered indirect costs.

children.label: Unrecovered indirect costs
description: Calculate for externally funded R&D only (preferably on a project-specific basis) using the appropriate cost rate — on-campus, off-campus, etc.
bullets: First, multiply the negotiated rate by the corresponding base.

content.label: All other sources
description: Other sources not reported above, such as funds from foreign governments, foreign or U.S. universities, and gifts designated by the donors for research.

content.text: This item is confidential. Please see the <button type="button" class="modal-link" data-modal-target="confidentiality">confidentiality statement</button>.

Responses to the confidential items are collected under a pledge of confidentiality and will only be used for statistical purposes. Information from confidential items is not published or released for individual institutions; only aggregate totals will appear in publications. In accordance with the Confidential Information Protection and Statistical Efficiency Act (CIPSEA) of 2018, 44 U.S.C. § 3561 et seq., and other applicable federal laws, your responses will not be disclosed in identifiable form to anyone other than agency employees or authorized persons. Any questionnaire item not marked as confidential will be available on a public use file. For the Federal Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2015, codified in relevant part at 6 U.S.C. § 663, your data are protected from cybersecurity risks through screening of the federal information systems that transmit your data, and by the information security program that protects the agency's systems and data from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction, pursuant to the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. § 3551 et seq.
The following items are confidential:

items: The sub-values of institution funds on question 1: institutionally financed research (row e1), cost sharing (row e2), and unrecovered indirect costs (row e3).

content.text: How much of your R&D expenditures reported in Question 1 did your institution receive as a subrecipient from another U.S. university or college?

items: The subrecipient for an award carries out the work but receives the funds from a pass-through entity rather than directly from the original funding source. Subrecipients tend to be the co-authors of publications, writers of technical reports discussing findings, inventors, etc.
Do not include contractor or vendor relationships. A contractor or vendor receives payment for goods and services provided. See 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart D Section 331.
